clue.text: Fleet is stuck

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a noun for ships, but it is the adjective meaning quick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both speedy, like a fleet runner, and firmly fixed in place, as with a ship stuck fast.

clue.text: Worked out to inspire man, a leader, nominally

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the outer word takes the others inside it

parts.note: figured out a sum, worked it out
a man is a he
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has calculated how to motivate a fellow who is only nominally in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspire' here means breathe in, the outer word taking in the rest; 'a leader, nominally' is not split, since the A is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurehead holds the top title without real power, so is a chief in name only.

clue.text: Quietly called nationalist out for expressive gesture

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: out says the nationalist's letter is put out of the word before it

parts.note: rung, as in rung someone up on the phone
N is the abbreviation for nationalist

explanation.surface: Someone muttered that a nationalist had been called out and responded with a gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called' is the past participle as in phoned, not shouted.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders to show indifference or doubt is a wordless gesture that conveys feeling.

clue.text: Secure cash in Boston to conserve church decoration

parts.note: to win is to secure, as a prize

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep safe, so the money word holds the church inside it

parts.note: dimes are ten-cent coins, cash in the USA
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone in Boston pockets money in order to preserve a church's ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: WIN, then DIMES holding CH. Boston stands for America generally, so the cash is American coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind chimes are hanging ornaments that tinkle in the breeze, a decoration for a porch or garden.

clue.text: I clean revolting Dutch supermarket

indicators.note: revolting means rising up and overturning order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A shopper complains about cleaning up a disgusting Dutch supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Iceland is a British frozen-food supermarket chain, not only the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is the name of a UK chain of grocery stores specialising in frozen food.

clue.text: American leaving waste around old city

indicators.note: around says the trimmed word is wrapped round the old letter
the American abbreviation leaves, departing from the word for waste

parts.note: detritus is debris, waste matter
US is the abbreviation for American
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An American walks away from rubbish lying round an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old city' tempts as the definition, but old supplies a single letter and city alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the large Michigan city famed for car manufacturing.

clue.text: Own new port

parts.note: to own is to have
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone takes ownership of a newly built port.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a harbour, a sheltered place where ships can dock safely.

clue.text: State nominates criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent out of their order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: The government puts forward a crook for office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' sits at the front looking like a verb meaning declare; it is the noun, a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty United States, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: Scandal, primarily, has destroyed band

indicators.note: primarily points to the first, primary letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked and broken up, so these letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A scandal has broken up a pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a group of musicians, but it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: Appallingly, tip a cent — a meagre amount

indicators.note: appallingly means dreadfully badly, so these letters are set out in poor order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A stingy customer leaves a one-cent gratuity: a shamefully small sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small, inadequate sum of money.

clue.text: Fish in jelly, 25% off

indicators.note: a quarter off a four-letter word means dropping one of its letters, here the first

parts.note: agar is a seaweed jelly used in labs and cooking

explanation.surface: Jellied fish sold at a quarter off, like a market bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: AGAR loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar is a long-snouted freshwater fish, also called garfish or needlefish.

clue.text: That is found in side streets

indicators.note: found in says the letters are discovered within the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters inside these two words

explanation.surface: Something is located down the side streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is the Latin behind the abbreviation i.e., meaning that is to say.

clue.text: Planet scenes with Earth deleted

indicators.note: deleted means struck out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: venues are scenes of action, places where things happen
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: Images of another planet with Earth edited out of the frame.
explanation.walkthrough: VENUES loses one E.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the second planet from the Sun, the brightest in the night sky.

clue.text: Scare female away, yes?

indicators.note: the female letter is sent away, removed from the word for scare

parts.note: a fright is a scare
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone checks they have frightened a woman off: done, yes?
explanation.walkthrough: FRIGHT loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagged on a question, right? asks for agreement just as yes? does.

clue.text: End it on a high: put oil on body

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and muddled, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Finish on a high note, then massage oil into your body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a high' reads as a cheerful phrase, but 'on a' belongs to the letters and 'high' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To anoint is to smear with oil, especially ceremonially, so anointed means having put oil on someone.

clue.text: Earl in colourful uniform gets shipment sent again

indicators.note: in places the nobleman's letter inside the uniform phrase

parts.note: red is a bright colour
E is the abbreviation for earl
livery is a servant's or company's uniform

explanation.surface: A nobleman in bright uniform receives a parcel being sent back out.
explanation.walkthrough: Livery is the distinctive uniform of servants or a company, so colourful uniform is a two-word phrase the nobleman splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A redelivery is a second delivery of goods, a consignment dispatched once more.

clue.text: Primate kept secret about love with minister

indicators.note: about says the word for kept secret goes round the other pieces

parts.note: hid means concealed, kept secret
love is zero in tennis, O
MIN is the abbreviation for minister

explanation.surface: A cleric's secret affair with a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: H(O MIN)ID. 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which fits the minister surface, but here it is the animal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A hominid is a member of the great-ape family that includes humans, a kind of primate.

clue.text: Some say cat gave birth in African port

indicators.note: some say means as people pronounce it, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: a mog is a cat, and to have had issue is to have given birth

explanation.surface: A cat had kittens in an African harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Mog is British slang for a cat; issue means offspring, so 'had issue' means gave birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mogadishu is the capital of Somalia, a city on the Indian Ocean coast with a busy harbour.

clue.text: Amphibian bit staff

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a staff is a long pole

explanation.surface: A frog or newt bit one of the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' reads as the past tense of bite and 'staff' as employees; both are nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval form of a frog or toad, so an amphibian in its youngest stage.

clue.text: Relatively worthless report about Republican

indicators.note: about says the file word wraps round the party letter

parts.note: a dossier is a file or report
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A report on a Republican turns out to be of little value.
explanation.walkthrough: D(R)OSSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is rubbish, so drossier is the comparative: more like rubbish than something else.

clue.text: Attack a German woman who eats people after removing the head

indicators.note: removing the head means taking off the first letter of the word for a man-eater

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German
an ogress is a female ogre, a man-eating giant

explanation.surface: A cannibal German woman bites people's heads off and goes on the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: OGRESS loses its first letter after A and G.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggress is to make an unprovoked attack, the verb behind aggression.

clue.text: Pick a fight with boy eating pastry dish

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the boy's word encloses the pastry

parts.note: a son is a boy
a tart is a pastry case with a filling

explanation.surface: A boy scoffing a pie provokes a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: S(TART)ON. Start on is British for confronting someone aggressively.
explanation.definitionFit: To start on someone is to begin attacking or criticising them, picking a quarrel.

clue.text: Break very overdue — it's after ten

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
ten written as digits, 1 and 0, looks like I and O
overdue means late

explanation.surface: Something is badly late: past ten o'clock already.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's after ten' places the overdue word after IO, and V comes first. Ten as IO is a crossword trick reading the numerals as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a rule or law is to break it.

clue.text: Contest extension in house inspection

parts.note: to vie is to compete, contest
a wing is an extension to a building

explanation.surface: Neighbours object to a house extension during the viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contest' looks like a planning objection; it is the verb to compete.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewing is a visit to inspect a property for sale or rent.

clue.text: Recommend drink close to home but American declined

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, so only that letter is kept
declined means turned down, so the American letter is refused and dropped

parts.note: advocaat is a Dutch egg liqueur
A is an abbreviation for American
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a drink near home, but the American guest says no.
explanation.walkthrough: ADVOCAAT loses one A, then takes the last letter of home. Advocaat is a yellow egg-and-brandy liqueur popular in Britain at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate something is to speak in favour of it, to urge or commend it.

clue.text: It's a surprise to have periodical stocked in Northern Irish town

indicators.note: stocked in means held inside, so the magazine word goes within the exclamation

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
mag is short for magazine

explanation.surface: A newsagent in a Northern Irish town is surprised to find a magazine on its shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: O(MAG)H.
explanation.definitionFit: Omagh is the county town of Tyrone in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: What a student might be when backing Muslim

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the phrase is read from its end

parts.note: in NUS: a student may be in the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A student could be Muslim, and supportive of it too.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' union body.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunni is the larger of the two main branches of Islam, and a follower of it.

clue.text: Smelled onions and weed regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Someone sniffed out the onions and the weed.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of each word are taken separately, and 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose is to sniff or smell something out, so nosed is the past tense.

clue.text: Memo from Conservative twat

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
in British slang, to twat someone is to hit them hard

explanation.surface: An insulting note sent by a Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twat' looks like a noun insult; here it is the slang verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a short note or voucher, a brief written message.

clue.text: Book house by ocean

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
an ocean is a sea

explanation.surface: Reserve a seaside house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like the verb to reserve; it is a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Far-right politician punched by wife for a second time

indicators.note: punched by means pierced by, so the wife's letter breaks into the politician's name

parts.note: Richard Tice, a leader of the right-wing Reform UK party
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A far-right politician gets hit by his wife yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: T(W)ICE. Richard Tice is a British politician of Reform UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Twice means on two occasions, so doing something twice is doing it a second time.

clue.text: Take action to employ soprano, moving forward

indicators.note: moving forward says the soprano letter is lifted from its place and put at the front

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
to employ is to use

explanation.surface: A company acts to hire a soprano, making progress.
explanation.walkthrough: USE has its S taken out and placed at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to take legal action against someone in court.

clue.text: Aim of a Kabaddi player is uncertain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in kabaddi a raider tries to tag an opponent and get back safely
second meaning: precarious, with the outcome in doubt

explanation.surface: Whether a kabaddi raider will succeed is hard to call.
explanation.walkthrough: Kabaddi is a South Asian tag game where a raider must tag defenders and return to their own half in one breath.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a risky situation whose result hangs in the balance; literally it is the raider's task.

clue.text: Irritable in overcrowded gym

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Tempers fray in a packed gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and nervous, quick to snap.
